pass_a_gloss: At once also keep watch on the solemn thing of the scripture, promising a multiplication and hundredfolding of brothers and offspring and parents and lands and dwellings; but a woman as wife has not been reckoned together with these. For it has not been stated: each one who let go brothers or sisters or parents or offspring or lands or dwellings or a woman on account of my name will take manifold; for in the rising up of the dead persons they neither wed nor are wedded off, but they are as the messengers, those in the heavens.
pass_b_english: At the same time, note the dignity of Scripture: it promises brothers and children and parents and fields and houses many times over and a hundred times over, but a wife is not counted along with them. For it is not said, “Everyone who has left brothers or sisters or parents or children or fields or houses or a wife for the sake of my name will receive many times as much.” For “in the resurrection of the dead they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like the angels in heaven” (Matthew 22:30).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 16); the old English was a digest. The old English made τὸ σεμνόν 'the holy multiplication' and cited Matthew 19:29 on the very saying Origen says is not written.
ὁὲ read δέ; αἷς οἱ ἄγγελοι read ὡς οἱ ἄγγελοι; „ev read ἐν.
'Wife', as the sense of the list requires.
